The path round a square is the outer square minus the inner: (40+2s)^2 - 40^2 = 160s+4s^2. The answer IS the border region of the (a+b)^2 area square - the geometric reading of the identity rather than a bare expansion.
A student wrote (x+3)^2 as x^2+9; the diagnosis is that the 2ab term 6x is missing. The error is precisely in the square-of-a-sum identity.

With b = -2 the item asks which statement is correct, and the wrong option D claims (a-b)^2 holds 'only when b is positive'. What is being tested is that an identity holds for ALL values of the variables - this concept, not any one identity.
(y+4)(y+7) = y^2+11y+28; the student had the ab term but not the (a+b)x term, so the missing part is 11y. That middle coefficient is exactly what this identity supplies.
